A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same FLAM research work, including the complete main text and Appendices A–C. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison support a reliable comparison of all 22 pages.

before.justification: v1 reports original sound-event detection, retrieval and zero-shot classification experiments in Section 5, plus qualitative results and ablations in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments, including the benchmark results in Tables 1–3 and appendix analyses in Tables 4–8.

M1.justification: FLAM's architecture, global and frame-wise objectives, text-dependent logit adjustment, inference procedure and memory-efficient training remain unchanged. The appendix equation corrections do not alter the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same training corpora and the same sound-event detection, audio-text retrieval and zero-shot classification datasets. No task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in corresponding experiments, including FLAM-Global, retrained MGA-CLAP and the comparisons involving published MGA-CLAP, LAION-CLAP and CompA.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendix C retain identical data splits, sample counts, model configurations, training budgets, preprocessing, evaluation metrics and testing procedures.

E4.justification: The calibration analyses, qualitative examples, alignment analysis and ablations of logit adjustment, initialization, global loss, closed-set training data and temporal resolution are all retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged, including Table 5's statement that all reported correlations have p-values below 0.01. No repeated-run, seed or uncertainty information is added or revised.

E6.justification: All numerical results in Tables 1–8 and qualitative outputs in Figures 2–9 are unchanged. For example, FLAM's ASFX-SED AUROC remains 81.23 in Table 1, and its alignment correlation remains 0.409 in Table 5.

T1.justification: Appendix C.1–C.2 corrects the initial denominators of Eqs. (15) and (17), replacing negative-class conditional probabilities with the required joint probabilities. Equation (17) also restores a missing comma between -1 and x. These repair intermediate probability identities; assumptions and final derived expressions are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about open-vocabulary localization, bias-corrected frame-wise learning, scalable data synthesis and preservation of global-task performance.

C2.justification: Interpretations and limitations are unchanged, including explanations of calibration and alignment, global-local performance tradeoffs, and limitations from corpus scale, fixed 10-second inputs and coarse temporal resolution.

D1.justification: Implementation and reproducibility information in Appendix C.4–C.9 is identical, including initialization, optimization, preprocessing and ablation settings. Project and dataset access information is also unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography and related-work positioning are unchanged. The mathematical corrections do not revise the stated relationship to SigLIP or prior audio-language models.

P1.justification: The marginal arXiv stamp changes from v1 dated 8 May 2025 to v2 dated 8 June 2025. The prose, terminology, headings and document organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–9 and Tables 1–8 retain identical content, captions, axes, legends, structure and placement. The equation corrections introduce no substantive layout change.

improvement.justification: v2 fixes incorrect probability denominators in Appendix C.1–C.2 and a missing separator in Eq. (17), improving the accuracy and readability of the supporting derivations. The benefit is limited because the final formulas, method, empirical evidence and conclusions are unchanged.
